Read and write native measurement record bundles

Source: R/record-io.R
record-bundle.Rd

A bundle is a new directory containing one fixed manifest.dcf and six fixed UTF-8 CSV or TSV files. The manifest selects only documented v1 file names; it cannot provide paths. Text values remain machine data, including values that spreadsheet software may interpret as formulas. Hashes detect accidental changes and do not authenticate a source.

Usage

write_measure_record(x, path, delim = c(",", "\t"))

read_measure_record(path, max_bytes = 100 * 1024^2)

Arguments

x

A validated measure_record.

path

A new directory path to write, or a directory containing a complete bundle to read. Existing writer destinations are rejected.

delim

A comma or tab field delimiter.

max_bytes

A positive whole-number byte limit for all files read.

Value

write_measure_record() returns the normalized destination path invisibly. read_measure_record() returns a validated measure_record.

Details

The reader checks the manifest, payload hashes, table schemas, row and column counts, and point references before constructing a record. Its byte limit applies to the actual total bytes read from all seven files.

Bundle version 1

The six fixed payload names have the selected .csv or .tsv extension. Their ordered headers are:

  • sources: source_id, source_name, source_sha256.

  • samples: sample_id.

  • injections: injection_id, sample_id.

  • channels: channel_id, channel_name.

  • curves: curve_id, injection_id, channel_id, source_id, axis_name, axis_unit, value_name, value_unit.

  • points: curve_id, point_index, location, value, source_row.

The metadata tables retain the corresponding schema in measure_record(). The single DCF manifest declares Format: measure-record, Version: 1, and Delimiter: csv or Delimiter: tsv. It also has -Rows, -Columns, and -SHA256 fields for each of the prefixes Sources, Samples, Injections, Channels, Curves, and Points: for example, Points-Rows. The reader accepts any order of this exact field set.

Empty cells in nullable text fields mean missing; literal NA text remains text. Numeric missing values are written blank, and the reader also accepts NA in numeric fields. Positive contiguous point_index values restore point order within each curve. Numeric fidelity is exact double equality after positive-zero canonicalization; arbitrary R attributes are not serialized.

The writer validates and stages files beside the destination, reserves a new destination directory, copies payloads without overwriting, then copies the manifest last. A failed copy may leave an incomplete destination without a manifest; the reader rejects it. Existing destinations are never replaced.

Examples

record <- measure_record()
local({
  bundle <- tempfile("measure-record-")
  on.exit(unlink(bundle, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  write_measure_record(record, bundle)
  identical(record, read_measure_record(bundle))
})
#> [1] TRUE
